chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Burayd al-Ajli said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he broke his fast for three days in the month of Ramadan. He said: 'He is asked: Is there sin upon you for your breaking of the fast in the month of Ramadan?' If he says 'No', then it is upon the Imam to kill him. And if he says 'Yes', then it is upon the Imam to severely beat him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for breaking the fast of Ramadan depending on whether the person admits to the sin or denies it?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the judicial discretion of the Imam in applying hudud for intentional fasting violations, distinguishing between denial and admission of guilt. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the severity of punishment—execution or severe flogging (nakth)—depends on the individual's acknowledgment of the sin, emphasizing the role of the Imam as the ultimate judge in such matters.
